pages.text: Lay out the several parts before beginning. Keep the barrel-maker's pieces apart from the stock-maker's, and gather the smaller fittings in a tray.$(br2)This is a fictional trade handbook for Minecraft. The voice is old-fashioned; the patterns and materials belong to Rustic Craft II.

$(bold)Read the plates$()$(br2)Each square takes one named item. Leave empty squares empty. Component forge recipes yield one item, including Gun Screws.$(br2)$(c)Firearms require Create Mechanical Crafters.$() Standard crafting tables serve only for individual parts. Finished weapons and ammunition require kinetic power.

$(bold)A word on state secrecy$()$(br2)All firearm assembly recipes are classified state secrets and hidden from EMI/JEI. Only authorized holders of this handbook know the exact patterns.$(br2)No starting gift or loot provides this book. An Imperial Administrator must issue it via state authority.

$(bold)Create materials$()$(br2)Press iron or brass ingots into sheets. Heated Basin mixing joins one copper and one zinc ingot into two brass ingots.$(br2)The alloy crafting pattern uses two andesite and two iron or zinc nuggets.

$(bold)Precision mechanisms$()$(br2)Begin with a Golden Sheet. Deploy a Cogwheel, a Large Cogwheel and an Iron Nugget, in that order. Repeat five times.$(br2)One attempt uses five of each applied ingredient and may give a byproduct. Count successful mechanisms before assembly.
